briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 9, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Weather Events and Their Intensifying Impacts
sections.content: The Korean Peninsula is experiencing extreme heatwaves due to a 'double heat dome' phenomenon, demonstrating the reality of a climate catastrophe [9], with heatwaves reaching 40 degrees Celsius penetrating the vulnerable segments of society [8]. Europe is also facing a dual challenge of severe heatwaves and prolonged drought [10], and domestically, livestock farmers are suffering severe losses, with over 2,000 insurance claims for heat-related livestock incidents reported in two months [36]. Climate change not only raises concerns about ecological disasters, such as the northward migration of insects [7], but warnings have also emerged that it can disrupt people's social connections, exacerbating loneliness [42]. Extreme weather events are spreading globally, with thousands evacuated in Canada due to 'out of control' wildfires [54].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts to address climate change are showing progress in various fields. Domestically, a business agreement for climate change response and marine environment research cooperation has been signed [3], Uljin is cultivating 'resilient rice' to respond to climate change [4], and peaches in Yeongdeok, Gyeongbuk, have shown potential for breed improvement by growing well despite drought [5]. Jincheon County is moving to become a carbon-neutral green growth hub and realize energy welfare [11, 17, 28], Osan City has launched customized carbon neutrality education for businesses [12], and Gwangmyeong City is expanding carbon-neutral culture in daily life by collaborating with small business owners to increase stores issuing electronic receipts [15]. Internationally, Yangzhou City in China is integrating heatwave adaptation measures into its urban planning [49], and a Massachusetts senator in the U.S. has introduced a $105 billion bill to protect healthcare facilities from climate change [51], demonstrating ongoing adaptation efforts.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Renewable Energy and New Momentum
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, the momentum for renewable energy transition is strengthening. In Jeju, a renewable energy-based data center operation project is being promoted [20], and Gyeonggi Province is actively supporting regional efforts, including securing 21.9 billion won worth of renewable energy projects in six cities and counties upstream of Paldang [21, 22]. SK is accelerating its business by passing the first regulatory hurdle for establishing a renewable energy joint venture [23], and Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) is attempting innovative approaches, such as promoting a solar power generation project utilizing bicycle paths [24]. Notably, the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) is once again focusing on geothermal energy as a '24-hour renewable energy' source, following solar and wind power [26], heralding an expansion of the renewable energy portfolio.

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Setbacks in Renewable Energy Infrastructure
sections.content: Despite efforts to expand renewable energy, challenges are emerging in terms of infrastructure safety and policy consistency. In Greece, a wind turbine collapse incident raised concerns about safety gaps in renewable energy infrastructure [31]. Furthermore, in the U.S., offshore wind leases have been canceled, and $4 billion in public funds have been invested to abandon renewable energy capacity [33, 34], leading to concerns that this could undermine global confidence in renewable energy investment. The controversy surrounding Amazon's plan to build the U.S.'s largest 'climate polluter' data center in Texas [19] highlights the discrepancy between corporate carbon neutrality pledges and actual actions, sending a warning message.

sections.title: 🌍 Climate Change Policy and Judicial Trends
sections.content: Policy and judicial movements to address climate change are also drawing attention. The government is promoting 'Green ABS (Asset-Backed Securities)' as a game-changer for climate finance, and post-verification is expected to determine its success [18]. Domestically, discussions on policy responses to climate disasters are ongoing, including the review of additional easing measures for the progressive electricity tariff system during heatwaves [38]. Internationally, the U.S. Supreme Court has decided to hear state-level climate change lawsuits [44, 48], which is expected to further increase the legal significance of climate litigation. India is attempting an unprecedented 'green growth gamble' to expand its GDP by approximately eightfold within one generation while simultaneously transitioning its energy and industrial systems to net-zero emissions within two generations [55], and its outcome is keenly watched.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing comprehensively covered the intensification of extreme weather events, various domestic and international efforts to combat them, and the challenges and policy discussions surrounding the renewable energy transition. This is a time that calls for continuous attention and effort to address the climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
